/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 05 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2740 (46)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4191 (94)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1956 (62)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1824 (-11)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1021 (5)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market closed with the BCI 182 5TC climbing by $851 to $38,013 despite a slightly softer tone across the Pacific and South Brazil. The C5 index slipped by $0.390 to $13.30, while C3 eased by $0.160 to $36.795. Pacific activity was relatively subdued, with just one miner in the market. Despite being the only major buyer, the miner was reported to have taken around six vessels. Bids initially emerged around $13.00, with offers in the upper $13s before fixtures were eventually concluded around the $13.30 level. Operators were notably quieter, and the overall tone was a touch softer. In the Atlantic, activity eased following a particularly busy Wednesday, when at least 15 C3 fixtures were reported between $36.00 and $37.00. With limited activity today, rates softened slightly, with talk of a fixture around $36.30. The North Atlantic, however, continued to display a positive undertone following recent stronger transatlantic fixtures. A Narvik to Turkey fixture helped push the C8 index up by $3,625 to $41,000, reflecting the continued strength in the basin. Overall, the market saw a more measured pace of activity today, with the Pacific and South Brazil easing slightly while the North Atlantic continued to provide support.
PANAMAX
Market fundamentals continued to shift across both basins today, with the P5TC increasing by $554 to $17,603 as sentiment improved. Trans-Atlantic rates recorded a notable improvement, with reported fixtures concluded above previous levels as sources describe tonnage supply tighter, especially off the West Mediterranean. Market sources also highlighted an increase in both trans-Atlantic and fronthaul enquiry, prompting Owners to revise their ideas upwards, while bids were said to be moving in the same direction. The Pacific also saw a marked improvement, with Australian mineral demand said by market participants to remain at healthy volumes. Sources described bid levels as moving higher as Owners revised their ideas upwards. The North Pacific was also reported to be relatively stable, although fundamentals remained more evenly balanced, with some suggesting that any uplift in rates was partly driven by stronger sentiment across other key loading regions. The Ocean Dream (82,201 2020) open Ube 8 November was reported fixed to Richland for an Australia to China trip at a split rate of $22,750 for South China and $23,750 for North China. The Yangtze Crown (82,092 2018) Maoming 6/7 November was placed on subjects for a Pacific round at around $20,000, although no further details were heard. Norden were reported to have fixed the Atlantica (81,145 2021) Yangpu 8/9 November at around $19,500 to $20,000 for a South Australian grain round. Period activity was also reported, with the Apollonis (82,917 2025) open Hibikinada 7 November fixing to Norden for 11 to 13 months redelivery worldwide at around $19,250 to $19,500.
SUPRAMAX
With the Eisbein starting tonight, this could be the end of the meaningful week and the 11TC average was down $142 to settle at $23,051, with negative returns everywhere except the US Gulf. Sentiment has turned in the US Gulf and offers are now higher, although the reported fixtures appear to be prior to this change in fortune, including reports of a 61,000-dwt fixed from the US Gulf to NC South America with grains at 20,500. Elsewhere the market is softening, as everywhere struggles without enough fresh enquiry to offer any sort of impetus. The Levante Spirit (61,323 2014) Kandla 6-10 November fixed a trip South Korea with HMM in the low $14,000’s and the Xin Hai Tong 29 (57,295 2011) open Dar Es Salaam 11-15 November was rumoured fixed basis delivery Richards Bay for a trip Pakistan at around $24,000 plus $240,000 ballast bonus, but the Charterer did not come to light. A Chinese Operator was said to have taken the TCLC Luzhou (61,693 2017) open New Mangalore about 12 November clean for one year, but further details are yet to emerge.
HANDYSIZE
It was another relatively quiet day, with sentiment remaining cautious across both basins. The BHSI closed at 1,021, while the 7TC average edged up by $74 to finish at $18,370. In the Continent and Mediterranean, brokers reported a continued positive tone, supported by increased fresh activity and limited available tonnage. In the US Gulf, a modest improvement in the cargo-to-tonnage balance lent some support to the market, with signs of an upward trend. A 34,000-dwt vessel was fixed from the US Gulf to East Coast Mexico with grains at $17,000, although further details were not disclosed. In the South Atlantic, activity remained sluggish, with ample tonnage and a lack of fresh demand continuing to put downward pressure on rates. Across Asia, the market remained subdued, with sentiment broadly flat. The Portaitissa (37,149 2011) open Zhousan prompt was fixed by Woohyun for a trip to the west coast of Central America at $18,750. Meanwhile, a 38,000-dwt vessel open in East Australia was placed on subjects for an outbound trip in the mid-to-high $20,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Australian Exports
In September, Australian iron ore exports rose 1.0 Mt year-on-year to 82.6 Mt, Australian Bureau of Statistics data show. Shipments increased to India (+0.6 Mt to 0.6 Mt), Vietnam (+0.5 Mt to 1.0 Mt), Indonesia (+0.3 Mt to 0.8 Mt) and Japan (+0.2 Mt to 4.4 Mt), which outweighed the fall in exports to China (-0.9 Mt to 70.2 Mt) and South Korea (-0.3 Mt to 3.9 Mt).
Meanwhile, Australian bauxite exports rose 0.2 Mt to 4.3 Mt in September, as shipments to China climbed 0.4 Mt to 4.3 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape saw a strong session, with Nov and Dec rallying sharply as momentum picked up throughout the afternoon. Nov opened at 36,000 before climbing to 37,500, with heavy afternoon volume around 37,000–37,250, closing at that level. Dec strengthened from 37,000 to 38,800, with substantial volume around 37,500–37,850 before a strong late rally, finishing at 38,750.
